races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
Bahrain Turf Club Desmond Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Audience
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for O'Meara and Keane, whose recent form figures of 0-0-9-2-3 suggest inconsistency at 7f; steps back to 8f here which suits on past evidence, headgear noted, but has only 12 wins or places from 15 runs on similar going — needs a strong pace to deliver a late run.|
runners_data.comment: Placed on each of his last two starts — third most recently, second two back — Audience has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 117 puts him top of the field on our figures; yet to score in recent starts, but the consistency and 18-day turnaround make him the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Chicago Critic
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this confirmed hold-up horse for Murtagh; decent place record (13 from 15 on similar ground) but the one win highlights how often he runs into places without winning — 40 days off could sharpen him but the 8f Leopardstown mile demands the front-runners set a true test.|
runners_data.comment: Chicago Critic has run over today's trip and going, rates 7 lb above his official mark on our figures, and 40 days between runs leaves him fresh enough to improve — the risk is that he's been winless in his last six starts, those three fourths suggesting he finds one or two too good.

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's four-year-old holds genuine hold-up tendencies (two wins, four places in 14 recent runs on similar going) but is displaced toward midfield in this map because more rearward types than positions exist at the rear; races with cheekpieces, and the 21-day break is fine — the real challenge is whether he gets cover in a field running harder than ideal for him.|
runners_data.comment: Cowardofthecounty arrives with solid recent form — a winner three starts back, third two starts back, and second last time out — keeping good company on the whole, and he has experience of today's distance and going. The main risk is whether his speed rating of 94 can match the very best here.

runners_data.name: Tokenomics
runners_data.note: Luke McAteer on this prominent-racing five-year-old for Marnane, who has a strong strike-rate over 8f on similar ground (3 wins, 4 places from 15); 39 days off is a mild query but form includes a recent win at this trip — will look to press the front-runners and could prove dangerous if the duel tires the leaders before him.|
runners_data.comment: Tokenomics showed a second two starts back but has since disappointed with a sixth last time out, and the 39-day absence adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 135 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Celtic Motif
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed front-runners for Joseph O'Brien; won over 8f on good ground last time and has strong place record at the trip (4 from 6 on similar going) — the key question is whether Sheridan can assert early enough to share or take the lead from Needle Match without burning all resources by halfway.|
runners_data.comment: Celtic Motif won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but she ranks eighth of nine on our figures with a speed rating of 76, making her hard to fancy at this level despite the recent winning form.

runners_data.name: Al Haarith
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle's three-year-old for O'Brien has won over this exact trip and going combination (1 from 5 on similar ground) and travels prominently — at OR 106 he is among the highest-rated in the field and should be positioned just off the duel, giving him the tactical option to kick from two furlongs out.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Al Haarith faces a stiff ask, and his patchy recent form — unplaced second time back before winning last time out — offers mixed signals. He has run over today's trip and returns on a handy 26-day break, but the rating gap is hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's three-year-old holds up for Aidan O'Brien and shows a win over 9f on good ground — the drop from longer trips suggests a potential stamina advantage over this flat mile, but six wins or places from nine on similar going and the absence of a front-runner's pace makes him dependent on others to create the right scenario.|
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back but sixth two starts back and only third last time out, Isaac Newton arrives with patchy recent form that makes him hard to fancy ranked seventh of nine. He has run over today's distance and going, and 21 days between runs suggests he's ready.

runners_data.name: Needle Match
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners Haggas's three-year-old who is the confirmed pace-angle — but 96 days off is the significant fitness flag, and its recent form (1-4-0 in only three career starts) is limited; if fit and fresh it could dictate, but the fitness concern over a sharp-surface mile is real.|
runners_data.comment: Needle Match landed a win three starts back but has since gone unplaced, and 96 days off the track raises fitness questions; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 128 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Sparan Nua
runners_data.note: Bolger's three-year-old with a T14 strike-rate of 2/3 runs prominently and has won three of its last four starts, all over longer trips (10–12f); stepping down to 8f is the key question — stamina reserves may compensate, but the trip shortening on good-to-firm ground could catch it out if the pace is truly honest.|
runners_data.comment: Sparan Nua arrives in cracking form, winning three of her last four starts, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main question is whether that third last time out signals any vulnerability at the top of the weights carrying 128 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Needle Match and Celtic Motif are the two confirmed front-runners in this nine-runner Group 3 over Leopardstown's flat mile, and with both drawn in a field of this size they will contest the lead from the outset, creating a genuinely honest, pressured gallop rather than a dawdle. Tokenomics and Al Haarith will look to press from prominent positions just off that duel, meaning the race is likely to be run at a tempo that suits horses who can travel fluidly in midfield rather than those who need to be covered up and produce a sustained late surge. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all occupy their natural positions — Cowardofthecounty is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield but will likely have to settle for a rearward berth given the shape, while Needle Match and Celtic Motif are best placed to actually control proceedings. The contested pace established by two genuine leaders on good-to-firm ground over a flat mile favours prominent-to-midfield horses with a sharp change of gear — specifically those who can travel close to the pace without being embroiled in the fight, and produce a decisive move entering the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Needle Match and Celtic Motif fight hard for the lead and burn each other out before the turn
scenarios.body: The pace duel between the two front-runners sets a demanding tempo that saps the principals, leaving the race to those tracking just off them in midfield who can switch and accelerate on the flat Leopardstown straight; good-to-firm conditions ensure the ground does not slow the tempo and rewards horses with clean action and tactical speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Needle Match Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Motif fails to match Needle Match's early stride and Needle Match settles into a controlled, uncontested lead
scenarios.body: Haggas's three-year-old, returning after 96 days, gets his own rhythm and dictates a measured pace from the front, allowing him to conserve energy and sprint clear in the Leopardstown straight before hold-up horses can get to him; Marquand's patience and the flat track are key enablers here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly strong enough that even the midfield horses are stretched, opening the door for deep hold-up horses to finish fastest
scenarios.body: Chicago Critic and Audience, both held up and carrying similar form profiles, can produce a powerful late run if the race is run at a searching gallop from flag to finish; however, their chances are tempered by their tendency to come from too far back on a flat mile where the straight is not especially long.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate rather than fierce and a prominent horse controls the tempo before kicking clear in the last two furlongs
scenarios.body: Tokenomics or Sparan Nua, both comfortable racing prominently, could benefit if the front two neutralise each other early without truly burning the field up, allowing a prominent tracker to cruise into contention and outstay opponents; Sparan Nua's winning form over longer trips suggests stamina reserves if the mile is not run truly fast.

watchPoints.text: Needle Match's 96-day absence is the defining risk in the race — if Haggas's runner returns less than fully wound, the pace duel disintegrates and the entire race shape changes; watch the market move and pre-race behaviour closely.

Celtic Motif will attempt to match Needle Match stride for stride from the jump — if Sheridan is instructed to lead at all costs, both front-runners could set an unsustainably fierce pace that benefits only the deepest closers at the rear.

Cowardofthecounty is a genuine hold-up horse operating out of its natural role in this shape; if the field bunches early and it cannot find a true rearward position, its style advantage is negated and the 0.92 style-fit discount applies with full force.

Al Haarith for O'Brien and McMonagle carries the highest OR alongside Audience and Needle Match at 106 but has the profile most suited to this race shape — watch whether he travels ominously just off the pace in the first half of the race as an indicator of trajectory.

Sparan Nua's T14 trainer stat of 2/3 is a small but positive signal for Bolger, and the horse's unbeaten run of three wins before its last run third warrants respect — monitor whether McDonogh sends it forward early to claim a prominent position over this shorter-than-usual trip.

races.name: Ballyroan Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's 7yo carries strong recent form (2nd at 14f on Good) and handles this trip well, but his natural style is prominent and with several rivals also wanting that position he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal — at 51 days off, freshness is not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and beaten in his last three starts, Ascending is hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable 135 lb; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a win and second in recent starts show he can perform when conditions click.

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: One of two confirmed pace-setters and likely to go to the front from the off; recent form is modest (form 332547) and his best finish in similar going is a 2nd at 14f, but his role here is to set the race up rather than win it outright — 47 days off, no obvious going concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Dallas Star has at least shown consistency at this level, finishing second and third in recent starts, though seventh last time out after 47 days off is a concern; he has experience of today's trip and going, but his rating suggests he faces a stiff task from the middle of the field.

runners_data.name: Ethical Diamond
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Mullins on this OR 118 horse who is a class above on ratings; three wins in similar going and a prominent style that allows him to travel within himself before quickening — the step back to 14f from his recent 12f runs is not a concern given his profile, though his last two outings (5th and 9th) need explaining.
runners_data.comment: Ethical Diamond landed back-to-back wins three and four starts back and a further success five starts back, showing real consistency at the top level; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is the primary concern after 47 days off.

runners_data.name: Gaucher
runners_data.note: Mullins also saddles this 7yo who has won twice on Synthetic/AW going and was 2nd at 10f on Standa; the step up to 14f on turf is a slight unknown — his form at this trip (4th at 16f on Standa) is moderate and the going switch to Good to Firm is a factor to note for a horse whose best runs have come on a different surface.
runners_data.comment: Gaucher brings strong recent form to this contest — a winner three starts back and second two starts back show he fires in this sphere, and experience over today's trip and going is a plus; the 51-day absence is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Green Impact
runners_data.note: Harrington's 4yo has been consistent in similar going (8 of 9 runs in Good or similar), placed 4 times in his last five, but has yet to prove he stays 14f — all form is at 9-12f and the extra two furlongs on fast ground is a genuine stamina question; 74 days off is the longest break in this field.

runners_data.name: Layfayette
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in the race; Colin Keane partnered him to wins at 12f and 14f recently and he has the profile to benefit most if the front-runners burn each other out — 9 years old but clearly in career-best form and handled Good to Firm conditions in his last victory.
runners_data.comment: Layfayette arrives here in fine fettle, a winner last time out and second two starts back, showing consistent form at the top of the weights on 135 lb; he has experience over today's trip and going, and a 48-day break shouldn't blunt his edge.

runners_data.name: Omni Man
runners_data.note: O'Brien's 4yo is a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that position today given the congestion ahead of him; his recent form is poor (6th, 9th, 8th) and his best runs came at shorter trips on Synthetic — the 14f distance and Good to Firm ground both represent stretches of his profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Omni Man faces a stiff ask here; a third four starts back offers some hope, but recent efforts of fifth, eighth and ninth make him hard to fancy, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner; a 3yo racing off 125lbs, he won at 10f on Soft and was runner-up at 13f on Good — stepping up markedly in class to Group 3 and facing older horses, his role is likely pacemaking rather than winning, though if the pace collapses after he leads he could steal a place.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Asakir's recent form reads poorly after finishing seventh last time out, and he has been off the track for 50 days; the one bright spot is a win three starts back, and he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Endorsement
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on this O'Brien 3yo who has been placed five times in eight runs and won at 12f on Soft; a prominent style suits a race likely to have a solid gallop, but his best form is at 10-12f and the 14f trip on Good to Firm is an open stamina question — his recent run (2nd at 10f on Good) was encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Ran well enough last time when second, and a winner two starts back, but the 49-day break is a query for a colt who must give weight all round; he has run over today's trip and going, though, which at least removes one unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Dallas Star and Asakir are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground, creating a genuine, honest gallop rather than a dawdle — this is not a race where either will sit and wait. Ethical Diamond, Gaucher, Green Impact, and Endorsement all want prominent positions behind them, meaning the early stages will be congested and the race will be run at a tempo that suits those with stamina and tactical versatility over a true test. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — Ascending and Omni Man are natural prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield as others take their preferred berths, with Dallas Star and Asakir most likely to actually secure the front two slots. This contested, honest pace over a staying trip on fast ground favours horses with genuine mid-race relentlessness and the ability to sustain a long run from 2f out — hold-up horses and those with a late turn of foot are best placed, with Layfayette the archetypal beneficiary and prominent types who can rate and quicken from a good position, like Ethical Diamond, also in the frame.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star and Asakir set a genuine contested gallop that stretches the field from 3f out, rewarding those who travel economically and hit the line strongest.
scenarios.body: The honest tempo drains those caught up in early positional battles and the race becomes a true test of stamina from the turn in; horses who rate midfield or just off the pace and sustain their run to the line are best suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of Dallas Star or Asakir breaks more cleanly, dictates a controlled rather than flat-out pace, and the chasing pack are slow to organise.
scenarios.body: A solo lead at a regulated pace can give a front-runner stolen ground heading into the straight, and with the going riding Good to Firm the surface rewards a horse who saves energy at the front; neither Dallas Star nor Asakir has the profile of a dominant leader but a favourable split could see one last home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to burn off the two front-runners but not so destructive that it empties the prominent horses, allowing one to pounce from 2-3 lengths off the pace.
scenarios.body: Ethical Diamond or Endorsement, both sitting handy behind the speed, get a clear run into the straight and use their class or recent form to cut down the leaders; Good to Firm ground rewards those who can quicken off a sound pace rather than grind it out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly contested and furious, burning up the front-runners and the prominent group early, leaving the race wide open for those held up.
scenarios.body: Layfayette, a genuine hold-up type with a recent course win and a patient jockey in Colin Keane, is the only true closer in the field who would genuinely benefit from this shape; note that Ascending and Omni Man, though mapped to midfield, are natural prominent types and cannot be relied upon as true late swoepers.

watchPoints.text: Dallas Star and Asakir will fight for the lead from the gates — watch for early crowding and jostling in the first two furlongs as prominent horses Ethical Diamond, Gaucher, and Endorsement also try to press forward, creating a traffic squeeze that could cause interference.

Ascending and Omni Man, both natural prominent types, are likely to be unable to get their favoured position in this field — watch for them to either use energy fighting for ground early or to be shuffled back under pressure, compromising their chance.

Green Impact has not raced beyond 12f and has been off 74 days — watch in the final two furlongs for any sign of the trip stretching him, particularly on Good to Firm ground which could quicken the tempo at a critical stage.

Layfayette at age 9 is the sole true hold-up horse and will need the pace to be genuinely strong to close the gap — if Dallas Star or Asakir dictates a steady early fractions, Colin Keane may find himself with too much ground to make up from the 2f pole.

Ethical Diamond's last two runs (5th and 9th) represent a dip from his earlier winning form — Ryan Moore's ability to position him close to the pace without getting involved in early battles will be a key watch point in the first half of the race.

races.name: Carnival de Leop Handicap

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with genuine ability — won over 8f on Good and placed at 7f on Good in recent outings; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is useful and the track/trip combination looks suited, though getting a clear run from the back in a 20-runner field is the obvious risk.
runners_data.comment: Dinamine won last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, so he arrives with some relevant experience; however, he was fifth one start back and has shown inconsistency in recent starts, and a rating of 57 gives him little margin over the field.

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with form figures of 40-000 and no placing in five recent runs; Alan Persse's 5lb claim is modest compensation, and finishing positions of 13th, 15th suggest the horse is struggling to land a meaningful blow in 7f handicaps on Good.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Imperial Dream nonetheless catches the eye on ratings — our figure of 68 ranks him second of 19 — and he has run over today's trip and going before, carrying 142 lb from stall 2 on a quick 19-day turnaround; the risk is that recent form has been consistently disappointing.

runners_data.name: Pete's Dream
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner with a recent win (1/8f/GOO) and strong trainer strike rate over 14 days (5/42); racing prominently is his role though he steps up from a hold-up tag with a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he is not perfectly suited to full control — the uncontested pace makes this less problematic than it sounds.
runners_data.comment: Pete's Dream arrives on the back of a win one start back and ran third last time out, showing improved recent form; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 22 days since his last run leaves him fresh — the main risk is whether 142 lb from stall one ultimately takes its toll late on.

runners_data.name: Wellwhatshappenin
runners_data.note: Long absence (139 days) is a significant flag given the fade-in-finish warning; placed at 7f and 8f on Standard, but no Good ground win in the past five and the layoff makes assessing fitness difficult — the finishing concern compounds the risk.
runners_data.comment: Showed a win and placed efforts earlier in his recent sequence, but unplaced last time and returns after 139 days off; has run over today's trip and carries 141 lb from stall 9, though a rating of 56 leaves him with ground to find on the top runners.

runners_data.name: The Blue Panther
runners_data.note: Placed most recently over 7f on Good (2nd) which is directly relevant form; races from off the pace and Nicola Burns claims 5lbs, giving the combination a punching-above-weight chance if the pace proves testing enough to create a late opening.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, The Blue Panther bounces back quickly on 12 days' rest and has experience of today's trip and going — his second last time out offers encouragement, though 140 lb from stall 20 may not help his cause.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: 10yo with course form at 7f and 8f on Good, fitted with tongue-tie; races prominently and has placed in this grade before, making him a natural tracker of Pete's Dream — consistency rather than dramatic improvement is the mode here.
runners_data.comment: Brains arrives here fit on a 12-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 64 puts him comfortably clear of his official mark — a second four starts back hints at better days; the concern is he's been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: Returns from a 246-day absence, which is a very serious flag at this level in a 20-runner handicap; DBM takes the ride which is a positive, but all recent form was at 6f on Standard/Hearthstead going and the step to 7f on Good is untested.
runners_data.comment: Gordon Bennett returns after 246 days off the track, and while he's winless in recent starts, that third one start back shows he retains ability; our rating of 69 heads the field, and experience over today's trip and going underlines his claims from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on a 4yo with a win on Good over 8f; races prominently and can sit handy to the leader, giving him a tactical advantage in a field of hold-up horses, though his best form has come over slightly further.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out offers encouragement, but a ninth the start before is harder to overlook — Launch Time has run over today's trip and returns after a 36-day break carrying 136 lb from stall 16, leaving him with plenty to do from a midfield ranking.

runners_data.name: Dress Dance
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse that the field size has pushed into a midfield mapping; fades in the finish and has placed just once (5th) in four runs, all on softer or Hearthstead going — the Good to Firm ground and the structural disadvantage of being displaced from her natural position both work against her.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and off the track for 79 days, Dress Dance faces a stiff ask from 135 lb, though she has run over today's trip before and draw three gives her a straightforward enough pitch from which to show more.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Recently won over 8f on Good at a lower mark and his headgear (tongue-tie/pads) is in place; a natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to field congestion, so he cannot race as freely as he would prefer — the STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 is the least damaging of the redistributed group.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and rated well below the field on our figures, Micasso is hard to fancy despite that win one start back; he has run over today's trip and returns after 25 days, but stall 14 and 135 lb make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: Best form has come over shorter (3rd at 6f on Good) and the step to 7f is a query; natural hold-up horse displaced from the rear by the weight of similar types, and the apprentice booking (Sadhbh Tormey, 7lbs) in a 20-runner handicap adds navigational risk.
runners_data.comment: Jazzit showed up with a third last time out and a third six starts back, but those eighths two and three starts back are a concern; he has run over today's distance and going, yet winless in his last six, he faces a stiff task from stall 8 off 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Cordouan
runners_data.note: Already noted above — see Cordouan note.

runners_data.name: Mogwli
runners_data.note: 9yo with a string of finishing positions in double figures (0-0000 recent); true hold-up horse mapped forward by necessity, and the form reads as a horse struggling to land a blow at any level — Megan Telford-Kelly's 7lb claim is the only positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 86 days, Mogwli faces a stiff task from stall 17 carrying 130 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 63 suggests more ability than his official mark of 47 implies.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: Form figures of 9760 with no placing in four runs; natural hold-up horse displaced to midfield, and Scott McCullagh has no visible positional advantage — trip and going are not obviously problematic but the form is the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts with finishes of ninth, seventh, sixth and unplaced, Pure Valour heads into this from stall 18 carrying 130 lb and ranks near the foot of our figures — experience over today's trip is the one box she ticks.

runners_data.name: Smaoineamh Sile
runners_data.note: 8yo with a 'U' (unseated/unusual) in recent form and a fade-in-finish flag; tongue-tie and pads fitted, and at OR 47 she is at the bottom of the weights — a true hold-up horse unable to race from her preferred position here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including an unseating two back and a ninth most recently — Smaoineamh Sile faces an uphill task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns fit enough on 21 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: Form of 00-000 with multiple deep-field finishes over 7f on Good — this exact track/trip/going combination has yielded 15th, 17th finishes; fade-in-finish tag and displaced from hold-up position makes her profile very difficult to support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and off the track for 94 days, Cannonball Queen faces a stiff task ranked 16 of 19 on our figures; she has run over today's trip before, and stall seven is her draw, but it's hard to build a case from a sequence of five unplaced efforts.

runners_data.name: Draiocht
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Soft and placed at 8f on Good, so she has talent — Wayne Lordan is a notable booking; hood fitted (first time?), a fade-in-finish flag applies, and as a displaced hold-up horse at 7f on Good to Firm (shorter than her best), conditions are not ideal.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Draiocht has managed just one win in his last five starts with two notably poor efforts sandwiching that success; he has run over today's trip and going, but from stall 19 carrying 126 lb, there is precious little here to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Best form over 10f and 9f on Good; natural hold-up horse mapped forward and the drop to 7f on Good to Firm looks sharper than ideal — Terry Casey's 7lb claim helps the weights but the trip shortfall is real.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Master Garvey ranks 15th of 19 on our figures and carries 123 lb from stall 12, making him hard to fancy; a third last time out offers a crumb of hope, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Has shown ability to place at 8f on Soft/Standard and can race in a prominent position; no jockey listed which is a concern in a competitive 20-runner heat, and form over 7f has been modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Desert Of The Sea faces a stiff ask here; three modest efforts since a brief purple patch of placed finishes are hard to ignore, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Suerte
runners_data.note: Ran just 3 days ago — very quick turnaround for a 4yo — and form figures (69-700) offer little encouragement; trainer Ms Lavery also has Dress Dance in the field, and the recency of Suerte's last run alongside a fade-prone profile makes this a difficult profile to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and back up just three days after her latest unplaced effort, Suerte faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip and going before and our rating nudges above her official mark, offering a sliver of encouragement from stall 10 at 139 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Pete's Dream is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to push him along — with Brains, Launch Time, and Desert Of The Sea the only other prominent types, the early gallop is unlikely to be truly searingly fast. On Good to Firm ground over 7f at Leopardstown, a controlled, front-running performance is entirely possible, with Pete's Dream able to dictate terms from a handy draw and control the tempo without being harassed. The field is packed with hold-up horses — Dinamine, The Blue Panther, Gordon Bennett, Suerte, and many others — but critically, runners tagged as redistributed (Micasso, Dress Dance, Jazzit, Cordouan, Mogwli, Pure Valour, Smaoineamh Sile, Cannonball Queen, Draiocht, Master Garvey) are natural hold-up types forced into midfield slots because the rear of the field is genuinely overcrowded, meaning those horses will not be in their optimal striking position. The dominant tactical verdict is that this race shape strongly favours a prominent or pace-pressing profile: with a lone leader setting a manageable tempo and the closers likely bottled up in a congested rear, horses who can race in the first four or five and quicken from there are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pete's Dream Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pete's Dream is allowed to bowl along uncontested and dictates a comfortable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Pete's Dream sets his own fractions on Good to Firm ground, and without genuine pressure the pace stays honest but not punishing, leaving him full of running into the final furlong. Prominent types who can track him — Brains, Launch Time, Desert Of The Sea — are the primary beneficiaries as they can pounce from close range while hold-up horses face a wall of traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Pressed, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Brains or Launch Time push Pete's Dream harder than expected, lifting the tempo enough to set up a prominent closer.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested gallop spreads the field and means Pete's Dream tires inside the final furlong, leaving those who tracked him at three to five lengths with a clear run to deliver their challenge. Horses with tactical pace and the ability to race prominently — Launch Time, Brains, The Blue Panther — are best positioned to capitalise as the front rank weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is true enough and the field fans wide late, creating a gap for a genuine hold-up horse to thread through.
scenarios.body: A fast-run race could expose Pete's Dream and the prominent brigade, leaving a clear late run available for the most tractable hold-up types — Dinamine, who has course form at this trip on Good, and The Blue Panther, who placed last time on similar ground, are the best placed to benefit. However, the overcrowded rear makes traffic and a clear run unlikely for most of the redistributed horses, meaning this scenario depends on a specific set of circumstances aligning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Wide Draw, Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes early scrimmaging, race falls apart positionally and an unconsidered horse strikes from an unpredictable position.
scenarios.body: With 20 runners and a field where natural styles cannot all be accommodated, a messy race could see some riders take a wide route for daylight, and a horse like Micasso — who has a win on Good and genuine ability when able to race freely — could emerge from unexpected positions. The redistributed runners as a group are at a structural disadvantage, but Micasso's STYLE_FIT tag is the most forgiving in this group and his form figures include a recent win.

watchPoints.text: Pete's Dream (sole front-runner) — watch whether Brains or Launch Time push him hard enough in the early stages to turn this into a truly run race or allow him to control an uncontested lead.

The 20-runner field creates significant traffic risk for the hold-up horses — watch the post-race draw positions and early scrimmaging, as Dinamine and The Blue Panther (the most credible closers) must get clear runs late.

Gordon Bennett returns from 246 days off the track — watch for any signs of greenness or sluggishness at the start, which in a 20-runner field could result in him being completely outpaced from the outset.

Wellwhatshappenin's 139-day layoff combined with a fade-in-finish warning is a key handicapping hook — watch whether she travels with her usual early enthusiasm or looks ring-rusty when the race begins to develop in the final 2f.

Suerte ran only 3 days ago — watch her odds movements and whether the trainer has a specific tactical reason for the rapid return, as quick turnarounds on Good to Firm ground can either sharpen or flatten a horse's response.

races.paceDynamic: Werifesteria and Sonic Invader are the two confirmed front-runners in a 25-runner field on Good to Firm ground at Leopardstown over 1m1f, and both are expected to press for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a dawdle. Werifesteria (Shane Foley, Harrington yard in form) and Sonic Invader (Colin Keane, Meade T14 strike rate 4/23) will push each other along, setting an honest pace that is likely to stretch the field early and leave little in reserve for either. This honest gallop on fast ground over a flat mile-and-a-furlong typically rewards horses who can travel prominently in behind the pace and accelerate through it, rather than those forced wide or waiting very late. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Guy's Girl, Wild Berries, Ohmali, Comfort Line, Darkdeserthighway, and others are genuine hold-up horses who will be shuffled into midfield by the sheer volume of traffic, meaning they will not be racing in their natural position; of those forced to take a closer pitch, Nibras Rainbow and Bella Colombia — both with prominent/handy-running profiles and good form at the trip — are best placed to exploit the pace set by the two leaders. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent hold-up types who can sit just off the leaders and pick up on the descent to the straight are favoured, while true hold-up horses pushed off their natural closing position face a material disadvantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pick Up
scenarios.trigger: If Werifesteria and Sonic Invader burn each other off at a strong early tempo, leaving them spent in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The two leaders set a searching gallop that bleeds the front runners dry, and horses traveling kindly in mid-division get a clean run to the line on the fast ground. Nibras Rainbow (strong sim-going record, OR=56 but progressive form 013213) and Bella Colombia (recent winner, good-to-firm handler) are ideally suited to picking up a weakening lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Duo Weakens, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not suicidal, allowing a prominent tracker to sit just off the pace and produce a sustained run.
scenarios.body: A horse like Tachos or Tequila, traveling in the slipstream of the leaders, kicks off the bend before the hold-up brigade can organise a challenge. Good to firm ground suits these types who can quicken off a true pace without having to make their effort from too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leaders Last The Trip
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is more measured than expected and one of the front-runners — most likely Sonic Invader with Colin Keane managing the tempo — conserves enough to last home.
scenarios.body: Sonic Invader, who has placed in long-distance races before dropping back, could prove better suited to this trip with a judicious ride, while Werifesteria on the Harrington form angle has the fitness edge at OR=66 with a handy weight. Fast ground and a flat track could allow a pace-setter to steal a meaningful advantage if the field is slow to respond.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Congested Finish, Chaos Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 25 causes traffic problems in the straight and the race is decided by a horse who finds clear daylight at the right moment.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types redistributed into midfield, the straight will be congested and a horse with a wide draw or a jockey who spots a gap early could steal it on fast ground. Darkdeserthighway (Dylan Browne McMonagle booking, experienced 8yo) or Comfort Line (recent 1st and 3rd, versatile) could benefit from a moment of fortune in the bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Nibras Rainbow — strong progressive form (013213), handles good-to-firm well, and races prominently, placing him perfectly to exploit the contested pace set by Werifesteria and Sonic Invader.
Sonic Invader ran on 22 days rest under Colin Keane but has only ever placed in stayers' company — watch whether he can genuinely sustain a front-running effort over this sharper 9f trip.
Werifesteria wears a hood for the first time today, which can alter a front-runner's early behaviour — if it unsettles her, the pace dynamic collapses and the shape changes materially.

Stepdance drops from 16f+ trips to 9f for De Bromhead after 69 days off — monitor in-running to see whether he travels prominently enough to be a factor before the straight, as his stamina profile is completely unknown at this distance.

The redistribution of at least 11 genuine hold-up types into midfield positions means the straight at Leopardstown is likely to be extremely congested — jockeys who find daylight early on the outside (Browne McMonagle on Darkdeserthighway) will be at an advantage over those trapped on the rail.

runners_data.name: Supreme Law

runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for a full year, Supreme Law faces a stiff ask off 147 lb, and his official rating of 40 underlines the size of the task — though our figure of 50 hints at marginally more ability than that mark suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Catalani and Miss Gitana are the two confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off over this 1m7f trip on good-to-firm ground at Leopardstown, creating an honest, competitive gallop from flag to finish. Catalani has shown front-running ability over extended trips and Miss Gitana has a habit of bowling along in front, though her tendency to fade in the finish is a known concern that could make the pace self-destructive for her. The field contains more hold-up horses than the track map can accommodate at the rear — Peace Walk, He Who Dares, and Supreme Law are genuine hold-up types forced into midfield positions because the back of the field is congested, meaning their natural style will be compromised. With two genuine pace-setters duelling over a staying trip on fast ground, this race shape most favours prominent racers who can sit just off the contested lead and sustain their effort into the straight — Chutzpal and Makaiah are the profiles to concentrate on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Catalani and Miss Gitana trade blows up front and honest fractions set up the race for a hold-position prominent racer.
scenarios.body: The duel between the two front-runners burns up the leaders over this 15-furlong trip, leaving the race wide open for a horse who has tracked them from second or third throughout. Chutzpal, with recent good-ground form over this exact trip and prominent racing style, and Makaiah, who has shown the ability to sit handy and finish, are ideally suited to this unfolding.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Catalani dictates a controlled lead and Miss Gitana fails to sustain her challenge, allowing the leader to coast in front.
scenarios.body: Catalani has won over extended distances on good ground and if Miss Gitana's known tendency to fade kicks in early, Catalani could be left alone to set a comfortable tempo and simply outstay the field. A solo lead over 1m7f on good-to-firm ground with no sustained pressure is the precise scenario that suits a horse who has placed twice over marathon trips.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compress the field and allow one of the hold-up types who lands in midfield to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: He Who Dares has won over 1m7f on good ground and Boxing Great has a staying profile, but both are racing out of their natural hold-up role having been mapped forward by the congested field. Should the pace prove truly searching and a gap open late, one of these misplaced closers could arrive with purpose, though their compromised positioning makes this a less reliable path to the winner's enclosure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse Of Pace, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners go too hard early and stop in their tracks, causing a scramble for positions inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A total collapse of the early pace would theoretically release the true hold-up horses Peace Walk and Supreme Law, but both carry significant concerns — Supreme Law returns from 364 days off track, and Peace Walk has no wins on this surface configuration. Even in this chaotic shape, the most reliable finisher from a prominent base, Chutzpal, retains claims.

watchPoints.text: Watch Miss Gitana in the opening half-mile — if she attempts to match Catalani stride for stride and the gallop becomes a duel, both front-runners could collapse turning for home and leave the race to Chutzpal or Makaiah sweeping through.
